title: Living with Charlie Parker on Vernon Avenue
summary: Parker moves in with him and Gene Montgomery in late 1945; Miles Davis and Stan Getz appear on the scene.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: And during this time, it was just about the time when Miles Davis came out here, because he was following Charlie Parker anywhere Charlie Parker went during that period -- and Charlie stayed out here. In fact, later on we lived together at a place down on Vernon Avenue just east of Avalon -- Gene Montgomery, the tenor player. We were living in the Civic Hotel, and we decided to move into this house, and Charlie came in there to live with us. This was just about the latter part of 1945, while I was still working... during the Christmas holidays. We were still working at the Streets of Paris, and they were still at Billy Berg's. And we were making all the jam sessions and everything.
Billy Byers was on the scene, the trombonist and arranger, and Warne Marsh used to come on the set and play.
He was just a kid, just coming around then. Stan Getz was a youngster, running around Hollywood with his saxophone, playing... That's where I first met him, was at the Swing Club.
